raw_response:
# C15 — Baseline B candidate answer

I found three useful mechanisms through opened awesome-list catalogues and then checked their primary documentation. One has versioned evidence before the 2014-04-07 cutoff; one is retained as later evidence; one has an unknown date. The translations below are inferences by an internal separate-context model, GPT-6 Astra Pro, not results from a human study or a different model.

## 1. GCC library builtins with ordinary callable fallbacks

**Use:** Treat selected operations as recognized ordinary library functions so direct calls can receive intrinsic lowering while function values and nonexpanded calls use an ordinary callable entry point without an ABI-adapter wrapper.

The [GCC 4.8.2 manual](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.8.2/gcc/Other-Builtins.html) identifies ordinary C library names as builtins and specifies a library call when builtin expansion does not occur. The [GCC 4.6.4 dialect documentation](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc-4.6.4/gcc/C-Dialect-Options.html) also separates recognition of a known function from whether a call remains in generated code.

For Rust, the transferable design is to retain an ordinary callable API while attaching intrinsic knowledge to direct calls. That can eliminate an adapter whose only purpose is a nominal ABI conversion. The function-value part is an inference from keeping real ordinary library functions: the retrieved manuals do not establish that every special __builtin_ spelling is addressable. This is a precedent for library-backed operations, not a universal solution for operations with special typing or immediate operands. It also does not promise intrinsic expansion or zero call overhead in unoptimized builds.

**Date:** Pre-decision. The [official release table](https://gcc.gnu.org/releases.html) dates GCC 4.8.2 to 2013-10-16 and GCC 4.6.4 to 2013-04-12. These dates support the versioned manuals, not the age of the live catalogue.

**Discovery catalogue:** [awesome-c, Compilers](https://github.com/inputsh/awesome-c).

## 2. MSVC intrinsic/function pragmas for dual implementations

**Use:** Associate supported ordinary function names with intrinsic behavior through compiler metadata while retaining real callable definitions for function values and calls that are not expanded.

Microsoft's [compiler-intrinsics overview](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/cpp-docs/blob/main/docs/intrinsics/compiler-intrinsics.md) distinguishes intrinsic-only routines from routines with both ordinary and intrinsic implementations. The [intrinsic pragma](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/cpp-docs/blob/main/docs/preprocessor/intrinsic.md) supplies compiler knowledge for named functions; the [function pragma](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/cpp-docs/blob/main/docs/preprocessor/function-c-cpp.md) explicitly restores an ordinary call.

The transferable mechanism is per-function recognition independent of an API adapter body. Restrict that inference to routines with genuine callable implementations; intrinsic-only routines do not thereby acquire function values. The [/Oi documentation](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/cpp-docs/blob/main/docs/build/reference/oi-generate-intrinsic-functions.md) makes substitution optional and documents semantic differences for some floating-point intrinsics, including exception and errno behavior. I did not execute a function-pointer or unoptimized-build test.

**Date:** Post-decision evidence. The opened documents have metadata dates 2016-11-04, 2019-09-02, and 2021-01-22. I did not establish this mechanism's pre-cutoff availability from a dated source.

**Discovery catalogue:** [awesome-llvm-security, MSVC Features](https://github.com/gmh5225/awesome-llvm-security/blob/main/README.md).

## 3. Clang builtin-alias attributes on intrinsic declarations

**Use:** Attach builtin identity to typed function declarations so public intrinsic names can be lowered directly after ordinary overload resolution, avoiding naming-only wrapper bodies.

The [Clang attribute reference](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AttributeReference.html), under clang_builtin_alias and clang_arm_builtin_alias, describes associating selected target-intrinsic declarations with an underlying builtin, including selecting the builtin after overload resolution. This is a useful representation technique for eliminating a source wrapper that exists only to connect a public name with a compiler operation.

Its present scope is restricted to selected ARM and RISC-V intrinsic headers. The documentation does not establish a general function-value mechanism. A Rust adaptation would still need to provide ordinary function types and ABI behavior, plus a callable implementation when a value is taken; simply attaching the alias attribute would not prove those properties or unoptimized performance.

**Date:** Unknown. This is a live undated reference; no dated release establishing availability by the cutoff was opened.

**Discovery catalogue:** [awesome-c, Compilers](https://github.com/inputsh/awesome-c).

## Design implication and limits

The useful separation is ordinary callable identity versus special lowering of a direct call. My design inference is to retain one ordinary function interface, lower recognized direct calls without compiling an adapter body, and provide a real callable implementation for function-value uses. These sources do not establish a complete Rust implementation or measured compile-time/runtime improvement.

HotSpot was a catalogue lead but was not retained without relevant primary verification. The catalogue also listed the C11 draft; three official-document requests timed out, so I omitted that candidate rather than relying on memory or snippets.

This run used 6 exact catalogue-directed search queries and 22 open/click attempts, including 6 failures. There were also 20 find operations within documents already opened. No compiler experiment or benchmark was run.

GCC's historical documentation supports ordinary-name builtin recognition and fallback, but addressability of every builtin spelling was not verified. Function-value applicability is expressly a transfer inference.
MSVC evidence is dated after the cutoff and is retained as later evidence. Clang builtin-alias evidence remains undated and is not asserted to be pre-decision.
